Issue #405 · Flevoland stap 2 · 16 november 2026

Componentenblad en ontwerpkeuzes

Hoe Flevolands huisstijl, geschreven voor publieke pagina's, werkt op een compact werkscherm. Alles op deze pagina komt uit fl-step2.css, gebouwd op Flevoland IT's tokens v0.2.0, plus vijf nieuwe tokens die hieronder benoemd staan.

Ontwerpkeuzes

One note per question in the brief: what we chose and why. Notes are in English, like the brief; UI copy is Dutch.

1. Type scale

Body, table and UI text: 14px (font-size-xs, Flevoland's smallest token). Secondary text, labels, counts, metadata: 12px (new token font-size-2xs). Form fields and section headings: 16px (sm). Form titles and the rail mode card: 20px (lg). Page and task titles: 24px (xl). 18px (md) only for the palette input. No size above 24px in the dashboard.

Today the dashboard runs at 11–13px with 9.5–10.5px labels. We move everything up one step and stop at 12px: nothing in the redesign is smaller. The 12px step is needed because metadata (dossier numbers, dates, counts) sits next to 14px titles in every row; making it 14px too removes the hierarchy, and making it a different colour alone is not enough. 12px is only used at weight 500+ or in text-subtle (#616161, 6.2:1) or darker.

Line heights: 1.3 (line-height-heading) for single-line UI (rows, labels, buttons) and 1.6 (line-height-base) for any running text: hints, messages, the assistant's answers. The 70ch measure applies to running text only.

2. Density

About 20% fewer task rows on screen (≈9–10 instead of ≈12 at 1440×900), the same number of rail items per group, and data tables at the same row count. Acceptable in the inbox; the swimlane and the Gantt keep their density by using 12px node metadata and horizontal scroll.

Measured in the prototype against today's CSS (Inter, same content): see Dichtheid below. Where it hurts most and what we did: task names may wrap to two lines instead of being cut off with an ellipsis (a deliberate trade: the full name is the information), metadata goes on one 12px line, and the filter and list columns narrow at 1280px. For the Infra-board Gantt and PA tables the rule is the same: 14px cell text, 12px secondary, 36px rows, compact 32px controls in toolbars.

3. Controls

44px stays the default for buttons and fields in forms, dialogs and every primary action (Flevoland, WCAG 2.5.5 AAA). One compact variant: 32px (new token size-control-compact), allowed only in toolbars, list headers, table rows, the filter bar, the dock and secondary actions inside a pane. Navigation rows: 36px (new token size-row), full-width. Nothing interactive below 32px; WCAG 2.2 AA asks for 24px.

The tab bar goes from 40px to 44px; the top-bar search is 36px; the avatar and icon buttons are 32px. Compact controls keep the 2px radius and focus ring, but use a 1px border (2px would take a quarter of the height). Forms keep Flevoland's 2px field border.

4. Fonts

Fira Sans for everything, Fira Mono only for technical identifiers (process keys, task IDs, raw JSON values, kbd hints). The serif logo becomes a Fira Sans 700 wordmark, "ronl." with a yellow dot, until Flevoland supplies a logo (open question).

Counts, dates and dossier numbers do not need a monospace: Fira Sans has tabular figures, switched on for the whole dashboard (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums), so columns of numbers still line up. Fira Mono is the same family and licence (OFL), so it adds no new style and no new provider. Both are self-hosted as woff2 (Sans 400/400i/500/600/700, Mono 400/500, 165 KB together); Inter, JetBrains Mono and Source Serif 4 and the Google Fonts link go away for Flevoland users.

5. Buttons

Primary = Flevoland blue fill (nl-button--primary), secondary = white with a blue 2px border (--secondary), ghost = link-coloured, no border (--subtle), danger = red fill (--primary --negative) and danger secondary (--secondary --negative). Yellow is no longer a button colour, except the floating "Vraag de assistent" toggle.

Today Flevoland users see yellow primary buttons (step 1 mapped the accent fill to yellow). The intranet uses yellow only for buttons in side columns, so the assistant toggle keeps it; every action in the work area uses Flevoland's blue button. Hover, active and disabled come straight from their NL DS mapping in base.css.

6. Focus and links

One ring everywhere: 3px #003a8e, offset 2px. White on the top bar and the tab bar (.flevoland-inverse). Full-width rows (rail, filters, task list, tabs, palette) draw the ring inset so it is never clipped. Links are underlined wherever they appear in text; navigation (rail, tabs, rows, palette) is made of buttons and is not underlined.

The tab bar is #003a8e, the same colour as the ring, so it must use the inverse ring (white on #003a8e: 10.5:1). Text links inside panes ("Bekijk het hele proces", the error summary, sources in the assistant's answers) are real links or link-styled buttons with the 1px underline, 3px on hover, purple when visited.

7. The ⌘K search hint

The search becomes a white field on the blue bar with #616161 placeholder (6.2:1), and the hint becomes a kbd chip: #424242 on #f5f5f5 with a #757575 border (9.2:1 text, 4.6:1 border). Was 3.78:1.

Focus op licht en donker

3px #003a8e with 2px offset on light surfaces (10.5:1 on white, 9.2:1 on a selected row). White on the top bar and tab bar. Inset on full-width rows. Tab through the prototype to see it live.

Badges en tellers

Status badges use Flevoland's status pairs (text 4.7–6.1:1 on their background) with a 1px border, 12px/600. Counts that ask for attention are yellow fills with dark text; quiet counts are plain 12px numbers.

Nu: 3,78:1 (faalt)

Stap 2: tekst 9,2:1, rand 4,6:1, placeholder 6,2:1

Nog open voor Flevoland IT

  • Is 14px body text, 12px metadata and a 32px compact control acceptable on internal work screens? This design depends on it.
  • Is Fira Mono acceptable for IDs and codes, or do they prefer their system monospace stack?
  • A logo or wordmark for the top bar, to replace the “ronl.” wordmark.
  • Who reviews, and in what form: this sheet plus the prototype, or a demo on acceptance?
